n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: People cannot worship Allah with anything better than asceticism from worldly pleasures.
Asceticism is the distinguishing characteristic of Godwary people and the natural disposition of those who turn to Allah.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Beware of wrongdoing for verily it corrupts your hearts.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: The wrath of Allah is indeed severe on one who wrongs somebody that has no one to help him apart from Allah.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Asceticism is not to prohibit oneself that which is allowed. Rather it is to find that which is with Allah more secure than that which is in one's own possession.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: The best of your youth are those who act like the old from among you, and the worst of your old ones are those who act like your youth.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Learning something during one's youth is like engraving in stone, and learning something when one is old is like writing on the surface of water.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Verily Allah, most High, boasts about the worshipping young man to His angels, saying, 'Look at My servant! He has abandoned his desires for My sake.

n: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), when asked to define the ascetic,
t: The ascetic is the one who renounces the permissible things in this world for fear of having to account for them, and renounces the forbidden things of this world for fear of punishment for them.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Visiting [each other] makes love grow [between you].

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Visit people at regularly-spaced intervals for that will increase love [between you].
Remember death frequently, for no sooner does man increase his remembrance of death than he begins to renounce this world's life.
If the inhabitants of this world used their intellect, the world would self-destruct [for it would cease to be of any importance].

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Verily venerating Allah' s Exaltedness involves honouring the old, the bearer of the Qur' an and the just Imam.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: He who sends peace and blessings on me once, Allah opens for me a door of vitality.

n: Imam Ali (peace be upon him), in what he wrote to Qutham b. 'Abbas
t: Sit for them in the afternoon, and give verdicts to the questioner, teach the ignorant, and remind the knowledgeable.
Meeting fellow brothers, even very briefly, causes the mind to broaden and develop.
When an abstemious person flees from people, seek after him, and when he seeks after people, flee from him.

n: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (peace be upon him)
t: Allah says, 'O son of Adam, be satisfied with what I have given you and you will be among the most abstemious of people.
Verily he who is most persevering in the face of adversity is the most abstemious from among you.

n: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (peace be upon him)
t: Every single believer whose eyes shed tears for the martyrdom of al-Husayn (AS) such that they roll onto his cheeks, Allah prepares chambers for him in Paradise as a result of them wherein he will dwell for ages.
Whoever recites a single verse of poetry about al-Husayn (AS), crying as a result and making ten other people cry, becomes deserving of Paradise and so do they.
He for whom the day of Aashura' is a day of grief, sorrow and crying, Allah, Mighty and Exalted, will make the Day of Resurrection a day of joy and happiness for him.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Ablution is half of faith.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: He who performs the ablution in the freezing cold weather is given twice the reward, and he who performs the ablution in the extreme heat is given a single share of the reward.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: When the Muslim man performs the ablution, mistakes committed by his hearing, his sight, his hands and his feet leave him so that when he sits, he sits forgiven.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: When the servant performs the ablution, his sins shed away from him just as leaves shed from a tree.
He who performs his ablution as best as he can and then walks to the mosque [is considered to be] in a state of prayer as long as he does not nullify it.
There is no prayer without ablution.
Ablution is one of the boundaries of Allah with which He knows who obeys him and who disobeys him.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Allah will resurrect my community on the Day of Resurrection among other communities, having white and illuminated faces from the effects of ablution.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Perform ablution frequently and Allah will increase your life, and if you are able to be in a state of purity throughout the night and day, then do so, for if you die in the state of purity, you will die a martyr.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: The man sleeping in a state of purity is as the man praying and fasting.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: He who performs ablution whilst already in a state of purity is given ten good merits.
He who renews his ablution without [the need to do so to purify] an impurity, Allah renews his repentance without him [needing to] asking for forgiveness.
Ablution upon ablution is light upon light.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Three things follow a person when he dies his family, his wealth and his deeds. Two of those retreat and only one remains his family and wealth retreat and his deeds remain with him.
He who lags behind as a result of his deeds will not be accorded a front position because of his lineage.
He from whom Allah accepts a single prayer, He will not punish, nor he from whom He accepts a single good deed.
If you act but a little, you will enjoy many bounties.
People transact through wealth in this world and through deeds in the Hereafter.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Just as grapes can never be harvested from thorn bushes, thus can the wrongdoers never come up to the level of the righteous, for they are two distinct paths, whichever one of them you take is where you will arrive.
Act continuously, act continuously! For verily Allah has not decreed any end to the believer' s actions except death.
The little that you perform continuously is weightier than the great amount that you perform odiously.
There is nothing more beloved to Allah than the performance of an action that is maintained regularly, even if it be little.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: The best of deeds is the most difficult of them.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: The best of deeds is that which is most regular, even if be something small.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: The best of deeds in the sight of Allah is the happiness that you bring to a fellow believer, either by driving away his hunger or by relieving him of his distress.
The best of deeds is that which you force yourself to do.
The best of deeds is that whose objective is Allah' s pleasure.
The best of deeds is adherence to the truth.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: There are three sins to which the company of a good deed is to no avail association of anything with Allah, insolence to one' s parents, and fleeing from the midst of a battle.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: He who does not guard his tongue has not performed any good deeds.
A good deed accompanied by doubt and denial is to no avail.
Allah does not accept a good deed from a believer as long as he harbours ill will against a fellow believing brother.
Be cautious of every deed which the doer is pleased to perform himself but hates Muslims at large to perform it.
s: Sharhe Nahj al-Balagha li Ibn Abi al-Hadid, v. 18, p. 41

t: Be cautious of every deed which is performed in secret but is embarrassing to perform in public.
Beware of any deed whose performance would be denied by its doer if mentioned to him.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Verily Allah, most High, loves for you to perfect a good deed when you perform it.

When Ibrahim, the son of the Prophet (SAWA) passed away, the Prophet (SAWA) saw a gap in his grave, which he filled with his hand, and then said, 'When any of you performs a good deed, he should perfect it.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Verily your deeds are exposed to me every day, and whatever good I see I ask Allah to increase them for you, and whatever bad I see, I seek forgiveness from Allah for you.
Verily the deeds of this community are exposed to Allah, most High, every single morning.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Verily Allah likes it for a believing servant of His, when he goes to visit a fellow brother, to get ready and adorn himself.
You should adorn yourself for your fellow Muslim brother when you go to visit him just as you adorn yourself for a stranger for whom you want to make a good first impression.
The adornment of your inner selves is more beautiful than the adornment of the outer.
The adornment of faith is purity of one's innermost thoughts coupled with good actions manifested outwardly.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: The best thing a man can adorn himself with is tranquility coupled with faith.
The best attire is that which enables you to blend in with people, which makes you look presentable in front of them, and which does not give tongues an excuse to wag about you.
No one can adorn himself with a better adornment than the obedience of Allah.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Allah Almighty said, 'The most beloved way that My servant can use to worship Me is through advising [others] for My sake.
s: al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib, v. 2, p. 577, no. 16

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: The people who have the greatest status with Allah on the Day of Judgment are those who roamed the earth the most, advising His creatures.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Let the advice a man gives to his brother be the same advice he would give to himself.
Give sincere advice to your brother, whether it be good or bad.
It is obligatory for the believer to advise a fellow believer, present or absent.
You must advise Allah's creatures for His sake, for you will never meet Him with a deed better than this.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: As for the signs of the adviser, there are four: he judges with truth, gives the right due from his own self, accepts for people what he accepts for himself, and he does not transgress against anybody.
It is enough for a person … when advising, to prohibit what he would not accept for himself.
He who among people is the best adviser to his own self is the one who is most obedient to his Lord, and the most deceitful of people to his own self is the one who is most disobedient to his Lord.

n: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (peace be upon him)
t: Excessive advice calls for suspicion.
[Good] Advice from a jealous person is impossible.
Blessed be the one who obeys an adviser who guides him, and avoids a deviant person who misleads him.
He who opposes [good] advice will perish.
Follow he who makes you cry when he advises you, and do not follow he that makes you laugh while he deceives you.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: The evil deed to be punished the quickest is agression.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Wailing is an act from the pre-Islamic age of ignorance.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Among the hidden treasures of goodness are: concealing one's afflictions, one's illnesses and one's charity [from others].

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Afflictions are easy for one who is abstemious in this world.
s: Kanz al-Fawa'id li al-Karajiki, v. 2, p. 163

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: He who finds an affliction too great to bear should think about [the greatness of his affliction resulting from] my passing away from this world, and his own affliction will become easier to bear.
Increase your remembrance of death, the day that you will rise from your graves, and your standing before Allah, Mighty and Exalted, and your afflictions will become easier to bear.

Verily when someone dies, Allah sends an angel to the most grieved member of his family, who strokes his heart and makes him forget the agony of grief, and if it were not for this, the world would never again thrive.
Whoever gloats over an affliction that has befallen his fellow brother does not leave this world until he is tried similarly.
Whoever draws the sword of agression will be killed by it [himself].
Agression removes [Allah's] favor.
Agression leads its perpetrators to the Hellfire.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Every single Muslim that plants or cultivates anything of which humans, animals or birds may eat from is counted as charity towards them on his behalf.

The farmers are the treasures of mankind for they plant and harvest the good things that Allah has made grow. On the Day of Resurrection, they will occupy the best and nearest position [to Allah] and will be called the blessed ones.

There is no occupation more beloved to Allah than agriculture, and every single prophet that Allah sent down was a farmer except Prophet Enoch [Prophet Enoch (AS) is known as Idris in the Arabic tradition (ed.)] (AS) who was a tailor.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Alcohol and faith will never be together in the cheast or heart of a man.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Alcohol is the mother of all indecent acts and grave sins.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: All evil in its entirety has been gathered in one house and drinking alcohol is the key to that house.
Allah imposed…the abandonment of drinking alcohol in order to safeguard the intellect.
When the alcoholic one meets Allah, Mighty and Exalted, he will meet him as an idol worshipper.
The one who drinks an intoxicant, his prayers will not be accepted for forty days and nights.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: When one who drinks alcohol speaks, do not believe him, and if he proposes do not marry him, if he falls sick do not visit him, and if he dies do not attend his funeral, and do not entrust him with anything.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: The alcohol drinker is like sulphur, so keep away from him lest he pollute you with his stench for sulphur has a bad stench.
The ones who have quenched themselves in this world with an intoxicant [alcohol] will die thirsty, will be resurrected thirsty and will enter the Hellfire thirsty.
Allah did not prohibit alcohol because of its name, rather He prohibited it due to its effects, so whatever produces the same effects as alcohol is [treated as] alcohol.
Three things enable a servant to attain Allah's pleasure: persistence in seeking forgiveness, affability towards people, and frequent giving of charity.
He who dissatisfies his body earns Allah's pleasure, and he who is not willing to dissatisfy his body defies Allah.
He [Allah] has advised you to be Godwary in all things, and has made it the height of His good pleasure and His sole requirement from His creatures.
Allah's pleasure is linked to His obedience.

n: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (peace be upon him)
t: Verily the one who Allah is most pleased with from among you is the one who is the most generous towards his own dependents.
The sign of Allah's pleasure with His servant is the satisfaction found in the servant himself with all that Allah decrees, be it in his favour or not.

n: Imam Ali (peace be upon him), in a letter that he wrote to Muhammad b. AbU Bakr,
t: Try to the best of your ability not to displease your Lord by pleasing any of His creatures, for verily Allah can easily substitute a servant for another, but the servant has recourse to no other substitute for Allah.

Allah – exalted be His remembrance – has not obligated anything more difficult for this community than paying the alms-tax, and the downfall of the majority of people lies in [their failure to pay] it.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: If you want Allah to enrich your wealth then give the alms-tax from it.
Strengthen your capital by paying the alms-tax.
The giving of the alms-tax never diminishes wealth.
We found the following written in the book of the Prophet (SAWA): …When the alms-tax is withheld, the earth withholds all its yield of plants, fruits and minerals.
Verily Allah has fixed the alms-tax as a provision for the poor and a proliferation of your wealth.
When the alms-tax is not paid, livestock die as a result.

There are three types of people that are considered thieves: the one who refuses to pay the alms-tax, the one who spends his wife's dowry unlawfully, and the one who takes a loan with no intention to repay it.
He who refuses to pay [as meagre an amount as] a sixteen of a dirham in alms-tax may as well die a Jew or a Christian.
The zakat of power is equity.
The zakat of beauty is chastity.
The zakat of prosperity is goodness to one's neighbours and maintaining relations with one's kin.
Fast, for that is the zakat of the body.
Verily upon everything is its zakat, and the zakat of knowledge is to teach it to those who are worthy of it.

Good moral conduct is the zakat of bounties, intercession is the zakat of high status, ailments are the zakat of the body, amnesty is the zakat of victory, and all that you give out zakat on is protected from being snatched away from you.
He who pays the obligatory alms-tax at the end of Ramazan, Allah uses it to make up for any deficit in the alms-tax paid on his wealth.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Allah Almighty loves the highest and the most dignified of things and hates inferior things.
The worth of a man is according to the extent of his ambition.
He whose ambition is lofty his value is heightened.

n: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (peace be upon him), in a supplication,
t: I ask You for the most fair witnessing, and the most active of worship … and the highest ambition.
There is no dignity like great ambition.
Tolerance and perseverance are twins, and high ambition produces them.
Kindness is the product of high ambition.
Good action is a sign of high ambition.
Worries are proportionate to the extent of one's ambition.
Enthusiasm is proportionate to the extent of one's ambition.
Attract the dignity of dismay with far ambition.
He whose ambition is short, he will envy a friend in his blessings.
A disgraceful person has no ambition.
There are three things that hinder a person from seeking the lofty: low ambition, few stratagems, and weak opinion.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: He whose sole concern is his food, his worth is [equivalent] to that which he eats.
He whose sole concern is what enters his stomach, his worth is [equivalent to] what comes out of it.
How far away is goodness from he whose sole concern is his stomach and private parts.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Allah has commanded me to treat people amicably just as He has commanded me to fulfil the religious obligations.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Being amicable towards people is half of faith, and being gentle and kind to them is half of life.
The fruit of [strong] intellect is amicableness with people.
The security of this world and the Hereafter lies in amicableness with people.
Whoever is amicable towards his enemies is secure from war.
Whoever is not improved by the goodness of amicableness will be improved by the evil consequences [of the absence of it].
Moving mountains is easier than bringing hostile hearts together.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: The best of the believers is the one who is loved by the believers, and there is no good to be found in someone who does not like others nor is he liked by them.
O people, revere Allah, for man was not created in vain that he may amuse himself, nor has he been abandoned to futility that he may be vain!
The worst thing that life is wasted on is play.
Amusement brings discontent to the Merciful, pleases Satan, and it makes one forget the Qur'an.
Amusement corrupts the wills of determination.
Gatherings of amusement corrupt the faith.
The farthest of people from success is the one infatuated with amusement and jokes.
He whose amusement increases his intellect decreases.

n: Imam Ali (peace be upon him), describing a believer,
t: His time is always occupied.
A believer does not occupy himself with amusement lest he becomes negligent, and when he thinks he becomes sad.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Every kind of amusement is wrong for a believer except for three: his taming of a horse, his casting from a bow, and his foreplay with his wife, for they are [with] the truth.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: The best amusement for a believer is swimming, and the best amusement for women is the spinning wheel.
Allah Almighty created the angels from light.
Allah did not create any creation more [numerous] than the angels…
Angels do not eat or drink or copulate, rather they subsist through the breeze of the Throne.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Gabriel (AS) came to me and said, 'O Muhammad, how can we [angels] descend to you [people] whilst you do not brush your teeth, you do not purify yourselves with water after excretion, and you do not wash your knuckles [of the dirt on them].
Gabriel (AS) said, 'O Messenger of Allah, we do not enter a house that has in it a picture of a human, nor a house that one urinates in, nor a house that has a dog.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Anger is a smouldering ember [kindled by] Satan.
Rage is a type of madness because the one enraged feels regret later on, and if he does not feel regret, then his madness has become ingrained.
Anger is the key to all evils.
Anger is such that it destroys the heart of even the wise man.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: The Prophet (SAWA) said, 'Shall I tell you who is the toughest and strongest from among you? The one who controls himself when he is angry.
There is no strength like being able to repel one's anger.
He who has no control over his anger has no control over his reason.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Verily there is a door to Hell, the entrance into which will be reserved for one who vented his anger through committing an act of disobedience to Allah, most High.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: He who curbs his anger, Allah will curb His punishment from him.
He who suppresses his anger despite being able to vent it, Allah will fill his heart with peace and security on the Day of Resurrection.
What a good dose anger is for he who can swallow it …
Remedy your anger with silence, and your carnal desire through your reason.

He (SAWA) [i.e. the Prophet] never used to get angry over worldly matters, but when he did get angry for the sake of the truth, he was unrecognisable and nothing could restrain his anger until he had triumphed in his case [for the truth].
Doubt is the product of ignorance.
He who displays his ill-feeling towards the immoral people and gets angry for the sake of Allah, Allah will get angry for his sake and will render him well-pleased on the Day of Resurrection.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Do not hit animals on their faces for verily they praise and glorify Allah.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: No animal, including a bird or any other kind, is killed unjustly except that it will raise a complaint against him [the killer] on the Day of Resurrection.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Whoever kills a sparrow in vain, it will cry out to Allah against him on the Day of Resurrection saying, 'O my Lord, so and so killed me in vain and did not kill me for any useful purpose.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: If the oppression that you have committed towards animals is forgiven for you, then [realize that] you have been forgiven a lot [of your sins].

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Are you not God wary with respect to this animal that Allah has allowed you to possess?! Because verily it has complained to me that you keep it hungry and tire it out.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: May the curse of Allah be on the one who treats an animal harshly.
Verily a woman was chastised for the fact that she tied up a cat and left it till it died of thirst.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Allah despises the adulterous old man, the wealthy oppressor, the arrogant pauper, and the persistent beggar; He nullifies the reward of the bragging doner, and he hates the blatantly insolent liar.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Allah, the Exalted, despises anyone who is knowledgeable about this world, but ignorant about the Hereafter.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Allah despises anyone who is ill-mannered, swaggering [in his gait], frequenting the markets, a corpse by night, [sleeping] like a donkey during the day, knowledgeable about this world, but ignorant about the Hereafter.
Allah, the Exalted, despises the insolent man who is audacious [in committing] acts of disobedience.
The Prophet (SAWA) used to say, 'Allah despises the one who frowns at the faces of his brethren.
Allah despises the vile person who displays his vices publicly.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: The most despised, by Allah, from among you are those who roam about gossiping and separating brothers, and seeking out flaws in innocent people.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: The most despised by Allah, the Exalted, from among His creatures is the scholar who frequents the rulers.
The person most despised by Allah from among all His creatures is the backbiter.
The person most despised by Allah, the Exalted, is the overbearing scholar.
Moses (AS) said, 'O Lord! Who do You despise the most from among Your servants?' He replied, 'The one who [sleeps like] a corpse by night and is idle during the day.
The person most despised from among Allah's creatures is a man whose [sharp] tongue people are wary of.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Nothing is more despised by Allah than a full stomach.
s: Uyoun Akhbar al-Ridha (AS), v. 2, p. 36, no. 89

t: Three things deserve the antipathy of Allah, the Exalted: [excessive] sleeping without night-vigil, laughing without a cause, and eating on a full stomach.
Allah, the Exalted, despises gossip, wasting money, and persistent begging.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: You have been sneaked upon by the plague of previous nations: jealousy and malice.
Three things bring about malice: hypocrisy, oppression, and self-admiration.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Allah detests two sounds: [the sound of] wailing at a catastrophe, and [the sound of] a flute in the time of prosperity.

Beware of anxiety, for it cuts off hope, weakens action, and brings sorrow. And know that the way out [of trouble] lies in two things: resourcefulness where a stratagem exists, and perseverance wherever stratagems fail.
Overcome anxiety with patience, for anxiety erases [Allah's] reward and augments the catastrophe.
The worst expression of grief is screaming and wailing with loud cries, beating one's face and chest, tearing out one's hair; and a man who takes up wailing is a man who has abandoned patience.
The catastrophe is but a single one for the patient man, and two for the anxious one.
If any amount of arrogance enters the heart of a person, it will only bring deficiency to the intellect with the same amount of what entered it, whether it be a little or a lot.
Whoever is free from arrogance will obtain dignity.
Arrogance is the robe of Allah, and whoever wants to wrest Allah of any of it, Allah will throw him onto his face into the Hellfire.
I sought after humility and did not find it other than through accepting the truth. Accept the truth, for accepting the truth distances one from arrogance.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: The most hateful of people are the arrogant.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: The most distanced of you from me on the Day of Judgment will be the braggers, who are the arrogant.
How man surprises me! His origin is a sperm and his end is a carcass, and between these two he is a vessel for excrement, and he is still arrogant!
Only he who is vile is arrogant.
A person is arrogant or tyrannical only as a result of a [source of] disgrace he has in himself.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: I admire a man who brings something with his hands to please his family, which repels arrogance from himself.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Whoever milks his sheep, patches his own clothes, mends his own sandals, trusts his servants, and carries his own goods from the market is free from arrogance.
Allah obligated faith as purification from polytheism, and prayer as chastisement from arrogance.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Whoever is arrogant, Allah degrades him.
Greed, arrogance, and jealousy are all motives for falling into sins.
An arrogant person has no friend.
He who behaves arrogantly will never learn.
He who behaves arrogantly with people is degraded.
An arrogant person should not avidly expect good praises.

In Hell there is a valley by the name of Saqar reserved for the arrogant, and it complained to Allah about the extremity of its heat and asked Him to be permitted to breathe. So it breathed and ignited Hell.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: If a man trusts you with his blood [i.e. that you will spare his life] then do not kill him.
Adhere to sureties [that you are liable for] in all firmness.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: The Muslims are brothers, their blood is co-equal, those under them strive to secure their protection, and they are like one hand against their enemy.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Shall I inform you of the worst of Allah's servants? It is the rude and arrogant person. And shall I inform you of the best of Allah's servants? It is the weak, abased person.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Verily Allah gives succour to this community only as a result of [the presence of] the weak among them, their supplication, their prayer and their sincerity.
The term 'weak' cannot be applied to those whom the divine proof has reached, whose ears have heard it and whose hearts have heeded it.
Where there are several answers, the correct one will remain hidden.
Sometimes even the eloquent fails to come up with an answer.
He who answers regarding all that is asked is mad.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Backbiting is worse than adultery', at which he was asked, 'How so?' He replied, 'A man commits adultery, then repents, and Allah pardons him for it, whereas the backbiter is not forgiven until his victim forgives him.
s: al-Targhib wa al-Tarhib, v. 3, p. 511, no. 24

t: Backbiting is the attempt of one who is incapable [of doing better himself].
Do not backbite lest you become a victim of backbiting, and do not dig a hole for your brother lest you fall in it yourself, for you will be paid back whatever you put in.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Backbiting eats away at a man's faith faster than a gangrenous sore can eat away to the inside.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Whoever backbites a fellow Muslim man or woman, Allah neither accepts his prayer nor his fasting for forty days and nights, until and unless the victim of his backbiting forgives him.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Backbiting is to say something about your brother that he would not like.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Until when will you sidestep talking about the impudent person?! Disgrace him [through disclosing his insolent acts] so that people may be on their guard against him.
The one who listens to backbiting is as [bad as] the backbiter.

n: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (peace be upon him)
t: The right of the ears is to keep them pure from listening to backbiting, and from that which is unlawful to listen to.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: He in whose presence a fellow Muslim brother is talked about behind his back, and who does not defend him despite having the ability to do so, Allah disgraces him in this world as well as in the Hereafter.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: When one of you backbites about his fellow brother, he must seek forgiveness from Allah for that is penance for it.
Cowardliness is an affliction.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Allah, most High, is beautiful and He loves beauty. And He likes to see the evidence of His bounty on His servant. He loathes misery and pretending to be miserable.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Allah likes for His servant, when he leaves to meet his brothers, to dress himself well and to beautify himself.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Each one of you should trim his moustache and the hairs in his nose and he should groom himself for this enhances his beauty.
Dress up and beautify yourself, for Allah is beautiful and He loves beauty; and make sure it is lawful [beautification].

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: The bane of beauty is vanity.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: The best thing given to a believer is good character, and the worst thing given to a man is a corrupt heart in a beautiful figure.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Look for goodness in people with beautiful faces for their deeds are more likely to be good.
The beauty of a believer's face is a sign of Allah's care for him.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Beautiful hair is part of Allah's dressing [for you], so make sure to honour it.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Beauty is in the tongue.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: There is no beauty better than the intellect.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: There is no clothing more beautiful than good health.
Physical beauty is the outer beauty, and the beauty of the intellect is inner beauty.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Do not betray the one who betrays you lest you be like him.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: The one who betrays his trust is not from us.
Betrayal is the fountainhead of hypocrisy.
The believer is naturally disposed to all the traits except betrayal and lying.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Disclosing the secret of your brother is betrayal, so keep away from that.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: As for the signs of the betrayer, there are four: disobedience to the All-Beneficent, disturbance to neighbours, loathing his associates, and being close to tyranny and oppression.
The betrayer is the one who busies himself with [the affairs of] others and his today is worse than his yesterday.

Whoever from among our companions seeks assistance from one of his brothers, who does not exercise his full efforts [in trying to help him], then he has betrayed Allah and His messenger and the believers.
It is sufficient for someone to be classified as a betrayer if he is the trustee of a disloyal person.
The peak of betrayal is disloyalty to a beloved friend and the breaking of vows.
One of the worst forms of betrayal is being disloyal with things entrusted in one's possession.
Verily the worst betrayal is the betrayal of the [religious] community, and the most repulsive deceit is that of the leaders.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Weigh your food, for there is blessing in weighed food.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Blessing are in trading and transactions.
Blessings are multiplied with justice.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: He who does not see the bounties of Allah upon himself other than in his food, drink, and clothes, then his actions fall short and his punishment is near.
Praise be to Allah Whose extolment speakers cannot attain, and Whose bounties cannot be enumerated by those who count.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: There are two bounties that most people are tested with: free time and health.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: There are two bounties that people are ungrateful for: safety and good health.
He who lives in bounties is ignorant of the worth of the calamity.
Bounties are ignored as long as they exist, but when they go they [their worth] are known.
Embrace your bounties before their departure, for they will leave and testify against their owner with respect to what he has done with them.
Beware the fleeing of bounties, for not every runaway returns.

Meet bounties by embracing them, and plead for an increase in them by giving thanks for them, and know that the self is the most accepting of what it is given and the most depriving of that which it itself has been deprived of.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Allah has servants whom He has chosen for bounties. He establishes these in them as long as they distribute them to people, but if they withhold them [the bounties], He transfers them to other people.
The least of what you are obliged to do for Allah is to not use His bounties to commit acts of disobedience to Him.
Bounties only remain when accompanied by three things: knowledge of what Allah has made incumbent with respect to them, fulfilment of thanks for them, and striving with them.
One who is clement with his enemy is victorious.
He who economizes and is content, his bounties will stay, and he who wastes and squanders, his bounties cease to remain with him.
Observing justice and benevolence invites the continuation of bounties.
O son of Adam, if you see your Lord bestowing bounties upon you in continuous succession while you are disobeying Him, then be cautious of Him.
Very often a favoured person is gradually being driven [towards punishment] through these favours; and very often an afflicted person is being done good through his affliction.
Allah Almighty's gradual baiting of His servant is that He envelops him with bounties and eradicates thankfulness from him.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Allah loves to see the signs of His bounties on His servant.
Allah is Beautiful and He loves beauty, and He loves to see the sign of His bounties on His servant.
Indeed I hate for a man to have been bestowed bounties by Allah and to not show it.
Bounties are completed through humbleness.
Complete the bounties of Allah over you by having patience in obeying Him, and refraining from disobeying Him.

Bounties in this world are safety and a healthy body, and the completion of bounties in the Hereafter is entrance into Heaven. And as long as the bounties [of Allah] are not complete in a servant he will not enter Heaven.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Beware of bribery for verily it is sheer infidelity, and the briber will not even smell the fragrance of Paradise.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Allah's curse is on the briber, the bribed, and the agent between them.

The ruin of your predecessors lay in the fact that they deprived people of their rights and subsequently resorted to buying them back, and they handled people using unethical means, which they followed.
Accepting bribes as a judge or ruler is tantamount to disbelief in Allah.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: If it were not for the fact that it would inconvenience my community, I would have commanded them to brush their teeth before every prayer.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Ablution is a main part of faith, and brushing one's teeth is a main part of ablution.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Freshen your mouths by brushing, for verily they are the means to the Qur'an.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Gabriel continuously advises me about brushing teeth, that I really thought he would lay it down as an obligation.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Brushing one's teeth increases one's articulacy.
You must brush your teeth for it removes whisperings of the heart.
Brushing one's teeth brightens the eyesight, increases hair growth, and removes the tendency for frequent weeping.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Brush your teeth in a horizontal manner and not in a vertical manner.
Verily brushing one's teeth at dawn before performing the ablution is part of recommended prophetic practice.
The best of houses is the bathhouse for in it the Fire [of Hell] is remembered and [bodily] dirt is removed.
Three things destroy the body and may even kill it: eating [cooked] meat that has been left overnight, entering the bathhouse after overeating and having intercourse with the elderly.
Do not enter the bathhouse except after you have put something in your belly that will cool the heat of the stomach for that strengthens your body. And do not enter the bathhouse with a full stomach.
Going to the bathhouse every alternate day causes weight gain, and going every day causes the fat around the kidneys to melt away.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: The believers are brothers, their blood is coequal, and they are one hand against others, the most inferior among them is empowered by their protection [of him].
Many a brother was not given birth by your own mother.
A believer is the brother of another believer [as if] from his own mother and father.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Seek to increase your brothers [i.e. believeing friends], for every believer will make an intercession on the Day of Judgment.
Adopt [the friendship of] true brothers and increase in your acquisition of them, for they are an asset in times of prosperity, and a shield during afflictions.
Do not let your brother be stronger than you are in your amity for him.
Love brothers in proportion to [their] piety.
O Ibn al-Nu'mani If you want your brother's amity for you to be pure, do not make fun of him, do not dispute with him, do not exchange bragging with him, and do not vie with him in evil acts.
Brothers need three things among them – they either use them, or else dispute and hate one another – fairness, benevolence, and evasion of jealousy.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Looking at a brother you love for the sake of Allah, the Exalted, is [an act of] worship.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: A Muslim cannot acquire anything as beneficial as his embracing Islam than a brother he benefits from for the sake of Allah.
Love is purified through cultivating friendship for the sake of Allah.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: When one of you likes his companion or brother, he should let him know.
Ask your hearts about their amities, for they are witnesses that take no bribes.
Know the amity that your brother has for you in his heart through what you harbour of the same in your own heart.

Do not seek sincere amity from a man you have insincere sentiment for, nor honest advice from someone you direct your distrust towards, for another's feelings [lit. heart] towards you are similar to your feelings towards him.
If you want to cut off relations with your brother make sure to leave a place for him in your heart, so he can return to it one day when he so wishes.
How awful it is to cut off relations after having maintained them, to turn away after brotherhood, and to have animosity after amity.
A man who places his amity in the wrong place is bound to suffer abandonment.
Do not let your brother be stronger in his avoidance of you than you are in your maintaing relations with him, and do not be stronger in your harm to him than in your kindness towards him.
The best person is the one who maintains relations with one who cuts him off.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: The most scarce things at the end of time will be a trustworthy brother and a legitimately earned dirham.
The one you need to safeguard yourself against is not your brother.
The worst brother is the one who stays with you in your affluence and abandons you in your poverty.
Do not take for brothers or companions: the fool, the miserly, the coward, and the liar.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Allah, the Exalted, likes the maintenance of old brotherhood, so maintain it.
Choose the new of everything, but the oldest one from among brothers.
Your brother is the one who does not abandon you in difficulty, does not forget you at the time of trouble, and does not cheat you when you seek his advice.
A man who shuns his brothers for every lapse has few friends.
A man who does not befriend [anyone] unless they are flawless will have few friends.
Tolerate the lapse of your friend for the time of your enemy's attack.
Tolerance is the splendor of companions.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: The best of your brothers is the one who helps you to obey Allah, prevents you from disobeying Him, and orders you to please Him.
The best of brothers is the one with the least hesitance in offering [harsh] advice.
The most beloved of my brothers to me is he who confers my faults to me.
The worst of brothers is he for whom one [is made] to go out of one's way.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: When you see three traits in your brother, place your hope in him: bashfulness, trustworthiness, and truthfulness. If you do not see them, do not place your hope in him.

A man who takes a brother after careful selection is bound to have a lasting companionship and a firm amity, whereas a man who takes a brother without careful testing is bound to resort to the friendship of evil people.

Test your brothers with two things, which they must possess; otherwise avoid them, avoid them, avoid them: observing the prayers at their prescribed times and helping brothers during hardship as well as ease.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: A believer is a mirror for his believing brother; he stays faithful to him in his absence and spares him from what he would hate to see.

n: The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family)
t: Any person in my community who acts kindly towards his brother in faith, Allah will grant him the service of the servants of Paradise.
A man who honors his believing brother when he comes to [visit] him is, by doing so, honoring Allah, Mighty and Exalted.
